text: Behind her, a narrow doorway remained cut into the rock.
speaker: Narrator

text: No darkness showed within it. Only a pale gray surface, deeper than shadow, shifting as though pages turned somewhere beyond sight.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun rose.
speaker: Narrator

text: She took one step toward it.
speaker: Narrator

text: The scratch of the quill had stopped.
speaker: Narrator

text: Her body turned before she permitted it. She caught herself with one hand against the rock and stared at the sand near her feet.
speaker: Narrator

text: Don't look back.
speaker: Zik
note: Ninsun remembering Zik's last instruction. Exhausted irritation, not ceremony.

text: Zik's last instruction had been neither noble nor ceremonial. He had spoken it with the same exhausted irritation he used when she interfered with a measurement or refused to admit a corridor was unstable. The familiarity of it made obedience harder.
speaker: Narrator

text: She waited for footsteps.
speaker: Narrator

text: None came.
speaker: Narrator

text: She waited for his voice, for a hand against the stone, for the blunt scrape of his boots crossing the threshold. The wind passed between the rocks and carried nothing with it.
speaker: Narrator

text: The doorway narrowed by the width of a finger.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun pressed her forehead against the sun-warmed stone beside it.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Zik.
speaker: Ninsun

text: The gray surface inside the opening rippled once.
speaker: Narrator

text: Something struck the other side.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not a fist. Not a body. A single dull vibration traveled through the rock and into her hand, followed by the faint sound of a page being turned.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then the doorway folded inward.
speaker: Narrator

text: The edges met without grinding. The seam thinned, disappeared, and left an unbroken face of stone beneath her palm.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun remained there until the rock grew too hot to touch. When she finally lowered her hand, Enhedu's copper figurine had marked her palm, and Balag's axe head pulled heavily at her belt. She did not search the stone for another entrance. She did not call Zik's name again.
speaker: Narrator

text: She turned toward the desert with the City sealed behind her and began walking before it could decide to remember the door.
speaker: Narrator
